        cost = matrix[depot][r[0]] + matrix[r[-1]][depot]
        for i in range(len(r) - 1):
            cost += matrix[r[i]][r[i + 1]]
        return cost

    def total_cost(routes):
        s = 0
        for r in routes:
            s += route_cost(r)
        return s

    def reverse_route(r):
        return r[::-1]

    # ---- Clarke-Wright savings construction (capacity-feasible merges) ----
    # Initial singleton routes
    routes = []
    route_of = {}  # customer -> route index
    for c in customers:
        idx = len(routes)
        routes.append([c])
        route_of[c] = idx

    # Savings list
    # Deterministic: compute over all unordered pairs; tie-break by indices
    savings = []
    # Avoid quadratic over huge instances if extremely large; but training sizes are manageable.
    n = len(customers)
    cust_list = customers
    for a_i in range(n):
        i = cust_list[a_i]
        for a_j in range(a_i + 1, n):
            j = cust_list[a_j]
            s = matrix[depot][i] + matrix[depot][j] - matrix[i][j]
            savings.append((s, i, j))
    savings.sort(key=lambda x: (-x[0], x[1], x[2]))

    loads = [route_load(r) for r in routes]
    active = [True] * len(routes)

    # Merge routes based on endpoints
    # Keep route indices stable; mark merged-away routes as inactive
    for s, i, j in savings:
        ri = route_of.get(i, None)
        rj = route_of.get(j, None)
        if ri is None or rj is None or ri == rj:
            continue
        if not active[ri] or not active[rj]:
            continue
        li = loads[ri]
        lj = loads[rj]
        if li + lj > capacity:
            continue

        a = routes[ri]
        b = routes[rj]
        # Determine concatenation orientation so that i is adjacent to j after merge.
        # Valid if i and j are at appropriate ends.
        can = False
        if a and b:
            a_first, a_last = a[0], a[-1]
            b_first, b_last = b[0], b[-1]

            if a_last == i and b_first == j:
                # a + b
                newr = a + b
                can = True
            elif a_first == i and b_last == j:
                # reverse a + reverse b? Actually want i at end of A and j at start of B after merge.
                # If a_first==i and b_last==j, then reverse a so i becomes last; reverse b so j becomes first.
                newr = reverse_route(a) + reverse_route(b)
                can = True
            elif a_last == i and b_last == j:
                # a + reverse(b) so j becomes first
                if b_first == j:
                    pass
                newr = a + reverse_route(b)
                # Check: after reversing b, first becomes original last == j, OK
                can = True
            elif a_first == i and b_first == j:
                # reverse(a) + b so i becomes last
                newr = reverse_route(a) + b
                can = True

        if not can:
            continue

        # Accept merge
        routes[ri] = newr
        loads[ri] = li + lj
        active[rj] = False
        # Update route_of for customers in merged route
        for c in routes[rj]:
            route_of[c] = ri

        # Optional: compact after many inactive; but keep small to avoid complexity
        # (local search later will rebuild active routes anyway)

    # Collect active routes
    routes = [r for idx, r in enumerate(routes) if active[idx] and r]
    # Ensure all customers are covered (should be).
    # If some customers were not assigned due to rare issues, add as singleton.
    assigned = set()
    for r in routes:
        for c in r:
            assigned.add(c)
    for c in customers:
        if c not in assigned:
            routes.append([c])

    # ---- Feasibility repair (should be feasible already) ----
    # If any route violates capacity (shouldn't), split deterministically.
    repaired = []
    for r in routes:
        if route_load(r) <= capacity:
            repaired.append(r)
        else:
            cur = []
            ld = 0
            for c in r:
                dc = demands[c]
                if ld + dc <= capacity:
                    cur.append(c)
                    ld += dc
                else:
                    if cur:
                        repaired.append(cur)
                    cur = [c]
                    ld = dc
            if cur:
                repaired.append(cur)
    routes = repaired

    # ---- Local search: 2-opt within routes ----
    # Deterministic first-improvement.
    def route_2opt_improve(r):
        improved = True
        while improved:
            improved = False
            L = len(r)
            if L < 4:
                return improved
            base_cost = matrix[depot][r[0]] + matrix[r[-1]][depot]
            for i in range(L - 1):
                base_cost += matrix[r[i]][r[i + 1]]

            # Try all i<k
            for i in range(L - 1):
                a = r[i]
                b = r[i + 1]
                for k in range(i + 2, L):
                    if k == i + 1:
                        continue
                    c = r[k - 1]
                    d = r[k]
                    # Removing edges (a-b) and (c-d), adding (a-c) and (b-d) after reversing segment b..c
                    old = matrix[a][b] + matrix[c][d]
                    new = matrix[a][c] + matrix[b][d]
                    if new < old:
                        # Apply reversal of segment i+1..k-1
                        r[i + 1:k] = reverse_route(r[i + 1:k])
                        improved = True
                        break
                if improved:
                    break
        return improved

    # ---- Local search: inter-route relocate (customer insertion) ----
    def relocate_improve(routes):
        # Rebuild loads for safety
        loads = [route_load(r) for r in routes]
        any_improved = False

        # Try limited deterministic passes (no randomness)
        # For each source route, each customer, try best feasible insertion in any other route.
        # Complexity: acceptable for training sizes.
        rcount = len(routes)
        # Precompute route costs
        costs = [route_cost(r) for r in routes]

        for rs in range(rcount):
            src = routes[rs]
            if not src:
                continue
            Ls = len(src)
            for pos in range(Ls):
                cust = src[pos]
                ds = demands[cust]

                best = None  # (delta_cost, rt, insert_pos)
                for rt in range(rcount):
                    if rt == rs:
                        continue
                    if loads[rt] + ds > capacity:
                        continue
                    tgt = routes[rt]
                    # Evaluate cost change if remove cust from src and insert into tgt at position p
                    # Compute src removal delta
                    if Ls == 1:
                        src_removed = 0
                        src_delta = -costs[rs]
                    else:
                        left = depot if pos == 0 else src[pos - 1]
                        right = depot if pos == Ls - 1 else src[pos + 1]
                        old_edges = 0
                        if pos == 0:
                            old_edges = matrix[left][cust] + matrix[cust][right] if Ls > 1 else 0
                        elif pos == Ls - 1:
                            old_edges = matrix[left][cust] + matrix[cust][right]
                        else:
                            old_edges = matrix[left][cust] + matrix[cust][right]
                        new_edges = matrix[left][right]  # reconnect
                        src_delta = new_edges - old_edges

                    # Compute tgt insertion delta for each insertion position
                    # insertion position p means inserted before tgt[p] (p==len => at end)
                    Lt = len(tgt)
                    for p in range(Lt + 1):
                        # Determine neighbors around insertion
                        if Lt == 0:
                            tgt_delta = matrix[depot][cust] + matrix[cust][depot]
                        else:
                            if p == 0:
                                nxt = tgt[0]
                                old = matrix[depot][nxt]
                                new = matrix[depot][cust] + matrix[cust][nxt]
                                tgt_delta = new - old
                            elif p == Lt:
                                prv = tgt[-1]
                                old = matrix[prv][depot]
                                new = matrix[prv][cust] + matrix[cust][depot]
                                tgt_delta = new - old
                            else:
                                prv = tgt[p - 1]
                                nxt = tgt[p]
                                old = matrix[prv][nxt]
                                new = matrix[prv][cust] + matrix[cust][nxt]
                                tgt_delta = new - old

                        delta = src_delta + tgt_delta
                        if best is None or delta < best[0] - 1e-12:
                            best = (delta, rt, p)

                if best is None:
                    continue
                if best[0] < -1e-12:
                    # Apply relocation
                    delta, rt, p = best
                    # Remove from src
                    src.pop(pos)
                    loads[rs] -= ds
                    costs[rs] += (delta - (route_cost(routes[rt]) - costs[rt]))  # keep safe; will recompute later
                    # If src becomes empty, remove route
                    if not src:
                        routes.pop(rs)
                        # Update indices after removal by rebuilding
                        return True  # signal to outer to re-evaluate

                    # Insert into tgt
                    routes[rt if rt < rs else rt]['dummy'] if False else None  # no-op for determinism
                    tgt = routes[rt]
                    if p == len(tgt):
                        tgt.append(cust)
                    else:
                        tgt.insert(p, cust)
                    # Recompute loads and costs (simple and safe)
                    routes = routes
                    loads = [route_load(r) for r in routes]
                    costs = [route_cost(r) for r in routes]
                    any_improved = True
                    return True  # first improvement overall; deterministic
        return any
